target_customer: Companies whose employees build prompts, skills and agents that need sharing and governance (current product); B2B sales teams (original product)
problem: Useful AI capabilities built by employees stay on one laptop. Mica provides a managed internal marketplace to publish, discover, install, verify and improve them. The original launch product automated B2B sales follow up from call recordings.
product_category: AI capability distribution and governance layer; originally AI sales follow up agents

founders.name: Achyuta Iyengar
education: UC Berkeley Haas School of Business, BS in Business Administration
founders.background_notes: YC page: product manager at Lob (YC S13) leading new products, address verification and developer experience.

founders.name: Bharadwaj Swaminathan
education: UC Berkeley, bachelor's in data science and economics
founders.background_notes: YC page: data scientist building ML products for networking.

technical_complexity.rationale: Both products involve agent orchestration, integrations with call recorders or AI tools, and eval gating, which is standard LLM engineering with some hard reliability work.

defensibility.rationale: Sales call tools (Gong, Fireflies) could add follow up features; the newer capability marketplace depends on being embedded in company workflows, and similar skills marketplaces appeared in 2026.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not directly sourced; a 2026 listing shows separate skills marketplace products such as Shared Context, and no acquisition of Mica was found.

market_need_then: Sales teams record calls but follow up poorly; the founders built the first product around that gap. For the later product, the site's argument is that employee built agents die on one laptop, which is a company claim.

branding.domain_note: Uses usemica.com (use prefix); no purchase history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and confident with short headlines such as Stop letting good agents die on one laptop.

brand_strength.rationale: Search results show many unrelated companies called Mica, which makes the name generic and confusable, and no brand coverage exists.

pivots.from: AI agents that analyze sales calls and automate B2B sales follow up (YC launch post)
pivots.to: Internal marketplace turning employees' AI skills into shared company infrastructure
pivots.why: Not stated by a source; the date is unknown but the site footer shows 2026

outcome_analysis: Mica launched in the YC Summer 2024 batch with a sales follow up product and now presents a different product, a governed marketplace for company AI capabilities, with a three person team. The company site shows Y Combinator, General Catalyst and Zero Knowledge Ventures logos. No amounts or dates are public, so the funding trajectory and the reason for the pivot are unknown.
notes: The company site shows backer logos for Y Combinator, General Catalyst and Zero Knowledge Ventures without amounts or dates, so no round is recorded; a search for General Catalyst coverage of Mica found none. Aggregators list 500K USD pre-seed from YC in September 2024, unverified. Aggregators also describe Mica as data ops agents or a marketing content tool, which conflicts with YC and was ignored. A third co-founder named Jai appears only in the launch post, with no details, so he is not listed. Competitor search returned no dated sources near the batch. Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs. YC batch is Summer 2024. The 500K pre-seed of Sept 2024 rests on a single database (VCBacked, echoed by Startup-Seeker) and matches the standard YC deal; Latka claims no outside funding.
